name: Roberta Smith

said.q: Confronted with one of Twombly’s paintings or drawings, one is always struck by their sense of abandon. Their various combinations of scrawls, graffiti, paint smears, letters, numerals, words, word fragments diagrams and signs have the visual effect…of seeing 'an overeducated bibliophiliac suddenly—graphically, nearly obscenely—speaking in tongues.' Conversely, it can seem that a primitive or insane artist has got his hands on one of culture’s classics and is telling us what really happened in the most vivid and yet abstract sense
said.in: in Exh. Cat., Zurich Kunsthaus, Cy Twombly: Paintings, Works on Paper, Sculpture, 1987, p. 15
said.via: Sotheby's: Contemporary Art Day Auction, on Artsy

said.q: Rauschenberg’s art functioned as a kind of sieve in which he caught and brilliantly composed the chaotic flood of existing objects or images that the world offered
said.in: “An Artist of Selective Abandon,” The New York Times, 6 July 2011
